apiSecurityReview.scope: Research artifact only; application runtime is unchanged. Public getter and owned-object self-tests do not establish arbitrary pointer safety or general binding compatibility.
apiSecurityReview.leptonica: Removed pix_internal.h coupling. Seventeen scalar getters use public APIs and reject null pointers; 25 raw-array, reference-count/internal-capacity and ownership-ambiguous destroy accessors abort. The current worker uses TessBaseAPI JSON text results, not those Leptonica wrappers. The synthetic self-test owns all six object types locally and releases them through their matching public destroy functions for 100 cycles.
apiSecurityReview.patchContractTests: Four Python unittest cases, including changed/missing/duplicate/new binding and second-application rejection, execute before the isolated build. Native verifier checks valid public getters and all 25 denied calls; English/French worker smoke uses the same candidate.

compilerWarning.finding: The original fork lost its owned dawgs pointer on self-assignment and memcpy-copied a non-trivially-copyable object. The candidate now backports the exact upstream assignment method with explicit fields and a self-assignment guard, preserving original copyright plus an explicit modification notice. No casts suppress the warning. No CVE or exploitability is asserted.
